content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To season cast iron bbq grills and burners, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Remove stubborn rust with a wire brush (15 minutes)
Step 2. Apply a thin layer of flaxseed oil to the grates (10 minutes)
Step 3. Wipe off excess oil with a lint-free cloth (5 minutes)
Step 4. Place grates upside down in the grill (2 minutes)
Step 5. Inspect for even coating (3 minutes)
Step 6. Preheat the grill to 400 degrees (20 minutes)
Step 7. Allow grates to cool completely (1 hour)
Step 8. Reassemble the burner heat shields (5 minutes)
Step 9. Scrub the burner tubes with soapy water (10 minutes)
Step 10. Dry the burners thoroughly with a towel (5 minutes)
Step 11. Coat the exterior of the burners with oil (5 minutes)
Step 12. Vacuum out the bottom of the grill firebox (10 minutes)
Step 13. Check the propane tank level (2 minutes)
Step 14. Clear out the grease trap (5 minutes)
Step 15. Degrease the grill lid interior (20 minutes)
Step 16. Scrape the side shelves (10 minutes)
Step 17. Polish the exterior stainless steel (15 minutes)
Step 18. Remove debris from the ignition electrodes (5 minutes)
Step 19. Wipe the interior walls of the cookbox (15 minutes)
Step 20. Brush away loose carbon flakes (10 minutes)
Step 21. Organize all cleaning supplies on a tray (5 minutes)
Step 22. Wash the warming rack (10 minutes)
Step 23. Close the grill lid to trap heat (1 minute)
Step 24. Test the igniter button (1 minute)
Step 25. Check for gas leaks using soapy water (10 minutes)
Step 26. Soak the grates in a vinegar solution (2 hours)
Step 27. Rinse the grates with hot water (5 minutes)
Step 28. Buff the grates to a shine (10 minutes)
Step 29. Dry the grates in a low oven (30 minutes)
Step 30. Purchase high-smoke-point seasoning oil (30 minutes)
Step 31. Re-install the burner tubes (10 minutes)
Step 32. Apply oil to the warming rack (5 minutes)
Step 33. Clean the thermometer probe (2 minutes)
Step 34. Check the venturi tubes for spider webs (10 minutes)
Step 35. Wipe the control knobs (5 minutes)
Step 36. Empty the ash collection pan (5 minutes)
Step 37. Lay down a drop cloth under the grill (5 minutes)
Step 38. Gather all necessary hand tools (5 minutes)
Step 39. Brush the underside of the lid (10 minutes)
Step 40. Scrape out the drip tray channel (10 minutes)
Step 41. Light the grill burners (2 minutes)
Step 42. Remove the grates and flavorizer bars (5 minutes)
Step 43. Let the grill smoke for the first cycle (1 hour)
Step 44. Clean the side burner grate (10 minutes)
Step 45. Wipe down the propane hose (2 minutes)
Step 46. Apply a second coat of oil to the grates (10 minutes)
Step 47. Inventory the replacement parts (15 minutes)
Step 48. Clean the grill cabinet doors (10 minutes)
Step 49. Tighten loose bolts on the grill frame (15 minutes)
Step 50. Dispose of used steel wool (2 minutes)
Step 51. Inspect the burner ports for clogs (5 minutes)
Step 52. Clear the work area of flammable materials (5 minutes)
Step 53. Set a timer for the seasoning process (1 minute)
Step 54. Wipe the exterior handle (2 minutes)
Step 55. Record the maintenance date in a log (2 minutes)
Step 56. Scrub the flavorizer bars (15 minutes)
Step 57. Use a toothpick to clear burner holes (20 minutes)
Step 58. Clean the grease drainage tube (10 minutes)
Step 59. Verify flame color is blue (2 minutes)
Step 60. Check the casters and wheels (5 minutes)
Step 61. Heat the grill to 500 degrees for final bake (30 minutes)
Step 62. Apply protective wax to the exterior (20 minutes)
Step 63. Open the lid to vent smoke (2 minutes)
Step 64. Wash the drip pan (10 minutes)
Step 65. Wipe down the grill legs (10 minutes)
Step 66. Lubricate the lid hinges (5 minutes)
Step 67. Replace the battery in the igniter (2 minutes)
Step 68. Put on heavy-duty work gloves (1 minute)
Step 69. Inspect the gas regulator (5 minutes)
Step 70. Monitor the temperature gauge (15 minutes)
Step 71. Prepare a bucket of warm soapy water (5 minutes)
Step 72. Scrape the heat deflectors (10 minutes)
Step 73. Sweep the patio area around the grill (10 minutes)
Step 74. Re-install the flavorizer bars (5 minutes)
Step 75. Clean the infrared sear station (15 minutes)
Step 76. Check the manifold for cracks (10 minutes)
Step 77. Let the oil polymerize (1 hour)
Step 78. Remove the protective grill cover (2 minutes)
Step 79. Brush out the burner crossover tubes (5 minutes)
Step 80. Clear out old charcoal debris (10 minutes)
Step 81. Clean the tool hooks (5 minutes)
Step 82. Apply oil to the interior lid surface (10 minutes)
Step 83. Check the orifice for blockages (10 minutes)
Step 84. Perform a final safety check (5 minutes)
Step 85. Read the manufacturer's cleaning guide (15 minutes)
Step 86. Put on an apron (1 minute)
Step 87. Take a photo of the seasoned grates (1 minute)
Step 88. Replace the grill cover for storage (5 minutes)
Step 89. Unplug the rotisserie motor (1 minute)
Step 90. Re-seat the propane tank on the scale (2 minutes)
